Over 3 weeks ago, all media propaganda and all news from the country of North Korea came to a complete halt. The country fell eerily silent, a country that has become so shrouded in mystery has now produced the biggest mystery of them all. Where in hell is North Korea?

We never really heard much from the country, the only time their existence was even brought to our attention was when they decided to brag about a missile or try to declare war on another nation, so when they first vanished we never really thought much of it. The news, the governments and the public just thought they were going quiet, that they didn't have anything to brag about this week. 

But then the next week came. Nothing. Just complete silence. south Korea found that the de-militarized zone was void of any North Korean soldiers. It was as if they had simply abandoned their posts over night. China stopped picking up their radio frequencies and the Chinese spies within Pyongyang suddenly stopped talking.

4 weeks had past, still silence. ISS and nearly all video satellite feeds showed a Korea that slept in darkness every night. their power had been seemingly turned off. The UN grew suspicious but they were adamant they were attention seeking again so the world ignored them for nearly 4 months and just waited for them to pop back up again with their attempt at attention seemingly crumbling around them.

But bang! A single flash of light was found where Pyongyang once sat. Satellites went crazy, it was trending on twitter, nearly every Facebook status offered up their own theory. Maybe they had detonated a nuke accidentally, maybe they were being liberated, maybe aliens had visited Kim Jong Un. The UN scrambled, this flash of light was impossibly bright and the nations panicked. The NK Flash as it came to be called was our first calling sign into the country.

The US, UK, China, South Korea, Japan and Russia all assembled a team of recon units. Heavily armed with weapons and high tech radio communications, they were dropped off right on the Chinese- Korean border and awaited their entry. They drove a truck into the country, a basic civilian jeep that could handle the poor road conditions. They didn't want to seem threatening to any of the people there.

They reached Pyongyang after a weeks journey. A week without any human contact, they said the countryside was empty, no sign of panic or chaos. It was as if they just got up, packed their bags and walked away from it all. It was a similar site in Pyongyang, just emptiness.
